literal: Knowing that he was devoted to the Buddhist teaching, [Yiyun] often followed him to hear lectures; for this intimate friendship he went to every length.
idiomatic: Knowing Yuanhai was devoted to the Buddhist teaching, Yiyun often followed him to lectures; for that warm friendship he spared no effort.

literal: When Xiaozhao grew critically ill, he entrusted the succession to Gao Zhan.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao grew critically ill, he entrusted the succession to Gao Zhan.

literal: When Gao Guiyan reached the capital, Gao Zhan still harbored doubts about him.
idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan reached the capital, Gao Zhan still harbored doubts about him.

literal: Yuanhai sent an ox cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace to take part in the deliberations; he then joined Yuanhai and the others in urging [Gao Zhan] to take the throne, followed the imperial progress to Jinyang, and joined in the government of the time.
idiomatic: Yuanhai sent an ox cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace for the deliberations; he then joined Yuanhai and the others in urging Gao Zhan to the throne, followed the court to Jinyang, and took part in affairs of state.

literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Province, given rear-guard musicians—it was his home province; he bore himself loftily and at ease, his ambition fixed on an appointment through the evaluation and selection offices.
idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Yan Province and given rear-guard musicians—it was his native province. He carried himself with lofty pride, his hopes set on a capital post in the personnel offices.

literal: When he saw people presenting themselves, he would contrary to expectation assent and draw them in.
idiomatic: When petitioners came before him, he would assent against expectation and draw them in.

literal: He also said his leave was only temporary and he would not long remain in the province.
idiomatic: He also said his absence was only temporary and he would not long stay in the province.

literal: He already had nao-and-blowing musicians; when it came to touring his jurisdiction, both ensembles were used together.
idiomatic: He already had nao-and-blowing musicians; when he toured his jurisdiction, both bands went out together.

literal: He still wrote a letter to Yuanhai discussing affairs of the time.
idiomatic: He still wrote Yuanhai a letter discussing affairs of the day.

literal: When Yuanhai entered the palace he inadvertently dropped it; Palace Attendant Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized it—on this account Yuanhai grew gradually estranged, and Xiaozhen was made concurrent Secretariat Drafting Officer.
idiomatic: Yuanhai entered the palace and dropped it without noticing; palace attendant Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized it. Yuanhai grew gradually estranged, and Xiaozhen was made concurrent secretariat drafting officer.

literal: Moreover, when Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Yiyun in his province privately gathered men and horses and also stockpiled arms and armor, intending them for his own defense—he truly had no other intent.
idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Yiyun in his province privately gathered men and horses and stockpiled arms and armor for self-defense—he truly had no other design.

literal: Someone reported him; when Guiyan was captured, [Yiyun] was also listed among his partisans who monopolized power—for this he was recalled.
idiomatic: Someone reported him; when Guiyan was taken, Yiyun was also named among his partisans who had monopolized power, and for that he was recalled.

literal: Gao Zhan still credited his past loyalty, in the end did not punish him, and appointed him concurrent Minister of the Seven Armies.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan still credited his past loyalty, did not punish him in the end, and appointed him concurrent minister of the seven armies.

literal: Yiyun was by nature bold and unrestrained, taking pleasure in showing favor; for generations his family had been governors of this province, his house rich in goods, and many scholars in want he aided and rescued.
idiomatic: Yiyun was bold and unrestrained by nature, and took pleasure in doing favors. For generations his family had held the governorship of this province; the house was rich, and many needy scholars he rescued.

literal: Once he grew eminent, he indulged pride and extravagance, building a mansion grand and vast that was finished in no time.
idiomatic: Once he rose high, he gave free rein to pride and extravagance and built a mansion so grand it was finished almost at once.

literal: His inner quarters were foul and disorderly; the scandal ran through court and countryside.
idiomatic: His inner quarters were foul and disorderly; the scandal ran through court and countryside.

literal: When he was a gentleman, over official business he quarreled with Left Vice Director Song Youdao; Youdao publicly humiliated him, saying: "The poem 'The Male Fox'—for a thousand years it has waited for you.
idiomatic: As a gentleman he had quarreled with left vice director Song Youdao over official business; Youdao publicly humiliated him, saying, "The poem 'The Male Fox'—a thousand years it has waited for you.

literal: " Yiyun answered not a word.
idiomatic: " Yiyun answered not a word.

literal: Yet he was cruel and violent beyond what human reason can compass.
idiomatic: Yet he was cruel and violent beyond what human reason can compass.

literal: At home it was worst of all—children, grandchildren, and servants were often covered in sores and wounds.
idiomatic: At home it was worst of all—children, grandchildren, and servants were often covered in sores and wounds.

literal: He had a bastard son, Shanzhao, vicious to the utmost; he fornicated with Yiyun's maidservant, and after countless beatings Yiyun had a cangue put on him, tied him to a tree in the courtyard, fed him fodder, and only released him after more than ten days.
idiomatic: He had a bastard son, Shanzhao, vicious to the core; he lay with Yiyun's maidservant, and after countless beatings Yiyun put a cangue on him, tied him to a courtyard tree, fed him fodder, and only released him after more than ten days.

literal: In the night Yiyun was murdered by a thief—it was the knife Shanzhao carried; it was left in Yiyun's courtyard.
idiomatic: In the night Yiyun was murdered—it was the knife Shanzhao wore; it was left in Yiyun's courtyard.

literal: Shanzhao heard of the calamity and ran to weep; when the household found the worn sword, Shanzhao was frightened and fled at once, taking refuge at the Ping'en villa estate.
idiomatic: Shanzhao heard of the calamity and ran to weep; when the household found the sword, Shanzhao was terrified and fled at once to the Ping'en villa estate.

literal: Next day Emperor Xiaozong ordered Gentleman-of-the-Household Lan Zichang to go to the mansion and investigate.
idiomatic: The next day Emperor Xiaozong ordered gentleman-of-the-household Lan Zichang to go to the mansion and investigate.

literal: Some time before, Yiyun had newly taken in marriage the Lady Lu of Fanyang from the Shaoshi quarter—she had beauty and charm.
idiomatic: Not long before, Yiyun had newly married the Lady Lu of Fanyang from the Shaoshi quarter—she had beauty and charm.

literal: Zichang suspected Lady Lu of having done it with an adulterer and was about to put her to torture; Lu set out in full the facts about Shanzhao as told above—they then seized him, imprisoned him in Linzhang jail, and were about to execute him.
idiomatic: Zichang suspected Lady Lu of adultery and was about to torture her; Lu laid out in full what Shanzhao had done—they seized him, bound him in Linzhang jail, and were about to execute him.

literal: Xing Shao submitted a memorial: "This is great treason; Yiyun was moreover a court noble—the execution must not be carried out in public."
idiomatic: Xing Shao submitted a memorial: "This is great treason, and Yiyun was a court noble—the sentence must not be carried out in public."

literal: He was beheaded in prison and the corpse cast into the Zhang River.
idiomatic: He was beheaded in prison and the corpse cast into the Zhang River.

literal: The full text uses Zhonghua Shuju, November 1972, first edition Book of Northern Qi, as the base for this collation.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against Zhonghua Shuju, first edition Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
